plugins.description: Stream a live, interactive iOS Simulator into the thread side panel with serve-sim.
plugins.overview:
## What you get

A **Simulator (serve-sim)** button in every thread header opens a side-panel tab with a
live, interactive iOS Simulator. Click to tap, drag to swipe, type to send
keys, and use serve-sim's own toolbar for home, screenshots, recording,
rotation, the device grid, logs and Safari Web Inspector.

Pick a device (booted ones are listed first) and press **Start simulator**.
The plugin runs [serve-sim](https://github.com/EvanBacon/serve-sim) in the
background and keeps it running while you switch threads; **Stop** in the
panel toolbar ends it.

## Annotate

Press **Annotate** in serve-sim's toolbar under the device or **⌥⌘A**: the
live screen freezes in place and you click the element you mean. A blue box shows
its type, text, and `testID`; **↑** selects its parent. Write a note, press
**Enter**, and a pill such as `1 · Buy Pro` lands in the composer. Your agent
gets the note, the element's `testID` (React Native / Expo), frame, and a
screenshot with the element outlined. Needs [idb](https://fbidb.io).

## For agents

`bb serve-sim start|stop|status|devices|logs` controls the preview from a
shell, and the bundled skill shows agents how to drive the same device with
`npx serve-sim tap|type|button|gesture` while you watch.

## Requirements

An Apple Silicon Mac with Xcode, an iOS Simulator runtime and Node.js 20+.
The BB server must run on that Mac: the panel embeds serve-sim's preview at
`http://localhost:<port>`, so it works in BB Desktop, not from a remote web
client. No account or external service is needed; the first start downloads
serve-sim through npx.

plugins.description: Project icons in the sidebar rail. Click one to focus the thread list on that project.
plugins.overview:
Keep each project one click away in the sidebar's left rail.

## What you get

- An icon per project under Home in the rail: your own PNG, an emoji, or a
  colored monogram.
- Click a project to focus the thread list on it; click again to show all.
- Cmd/Ctrl-click a project to start a new thread there; New thread in the
  header files new threads in the focused project.
- A dot on each icon when a thread in that project needs input, failed, is
  unread, or is working.
- Drag icons to reorder projects. Right-click an icon to move it, hide it
  from the rail, or give the project a home page: a plugin panel that opens
  when you click the icon.
- Home shows threads grouped by project, or one list with each thread's
  project icon.

## How it works

Focusing drives bb's built-in Thread list through its preferences: organize by
project and hide other projects into More. Showing all restores your previous
layout. Icons live in this plugin's storage; nothing leaves the machine.

plugins.description: Give projects their own Claude login off the Account Pooler, and see which account serves each thread with its usage limits.
plugins.overview:
Give some projects their own Claude or Codex login while the Account Pooler
keeps serving the rest.

## What you get

- Every thread of a listed project bypasses the Account Pooler automatically:
  new threads, resumed ones, and threads that already existed.
- Combine it with project environment variables (for example
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) to point those threads at a separate login.
- A chip in every Claude Code and Codex thread header and in the new-thread
  composer: which account serves the project (its own login or the Account
  Pooler) with a dot and the fullest window's percentage. Click it for the
  5-hour, weekly and per-model windows with reset times.
- Project logins appear in the Provider usage panel under "Project logins".

plugins.description: Browse a thread's workspace as a Cursor-style file tree with Seti icons and git colors, right in the side panel.
plugins.overview:
Browse the thread's workspace as a Cursor / VS Code style file tree in the
side panel.

## What you get

- **Files** in the side panel's Actions list opens the tree: folders first,
  ignored entries dimmed, Seti file icons like Cursor and VS Code.
- Also on the New thread screen, before the thread exists: it shows the
  folder of the project and environment selected in the composer.
- Git colors and letters for modified, added, untracked and conflicted files,
  with a dot on folders that contain changes, kept up to date while you work.
- Click a file to preview it next to the tree with bb's own preview; double-
  click, or click in a narrow panel, to open it as a regular file tab.
- Arrow keys and Enter move through the tree; expanded folders are
  remembered per environment.

Reads workspaces on the bb server's own machine.
